https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aae05893-33ff-4bef-8b62-bb4aca202056

Looks great! This is some much needed stuff in the editor.

Though I wonder if the terminology `Install Locally` and `Install Globally` could be confusing. Minor nitpick though.

I say this because "locally" could also be interpreted as "on this system", which both options do anyway.

> Though I wonder if the terminology `Install Locally` and `Install Globally` could be confusing. Minor nitpick though.
> 
> I say this because "locally" could also be interpreted as "on this system", which both options do anyway.

Perhaps it could be changed to `Install editor-wide` vs. `Install project-wide`, or `Install in Editor` vs. `Install in Project`. I think I prefer the former option.

### Update: Changed the "Install globally/locally" to "Install as Editor/Project-wide". Other "Editor/Project" terms also added "-wide" to it. But at some place it kind of look messy:
Also, changed the term "Compatibility" to "Scope", because thats sounded better to me, its like the scope of the plugin, to be for editor-wide, project-wide, or both.
Minor naming nitpick, but I think `Install for this Project` and `Install for all Projects` might be clearer specially for non-native English speakers, where the "wide" part might be confusing

> Minor naming nitpick, but I think `Install for this Project` and `Install for all Projects` might be clearer specially for non-native English speakers, where the "wide" part might be confusing

I can agree that does sounds easier to understand. But, maybe it's just me, but my concern of using this is that it sounds like the plugin will work the same way no matter which option you choose. Not editor-only vs. project (editor + running game). 

Still, I guess this concern can be eliminated by just adding a proper tooltip description to the options. So that's probably what I will do.

From testing (I'll be updating this comment as I find more problems): - [x] The empty column should be removed. EDIT: Ah, it's for warnings. Still weird though. Since we don't have a way to remove titles for single columns, maybe this should be integrated in the Enabled column instead? You can add the warning as a button next to the checkbox. Like this: Although Tree doesn't seem to handle longer text correctly. - [x] The state of "Show editor directory" button is not remembered between editor sessions (it should be stored in project metadata) - [ ] Duplicating a file into `editor://` folder causes duplicate UID warning (tested with `icon.svg`). EDIT: Still not fixed. Now there are progress dialog errors. - [ ] For some reason, global scene changes are not correctly propagated. Testing: open editor twice, edit a scene in one editor instance (it should be a main screen or a dock, something that gets instantiated in the editor), in the other instance reload the global plugin. The plugin reloads with old scene, _unless_ you have that scene currently opened. EDIT: > Haven't tested but this one may also be fixed since it looks like a similar issue with the previous one on this list: Still not fixed. - [x] Why is it possible to create global plugins from project settings? Why editor plugin is a default? In Project Settings it should not be possible to create Editor-only plugins and vice versa. - [x] This results in error spam at runtime: > The directory edit at the top can edit the path prefix between "editor://" and "res://". Not sure it this is going to break anything. Ideally it should be only available in EditorFileDialog, maybe as a button that toggles scopes. Or you can just remove it, FileSystem dock should be enough for file management (I assume you added it for options like Open Scene etc.) - [x] The Editor Plugins section should be hidden in the main settings - [x] Favoriting `editor://` files is broken. The filename is missing one character and the files are being wrongly modulated. - [x] Using the Move/Duplicate dialog in FileSystem freezes the editor. - [x] The editor does not remember uncollapsed paths in `editor://`. Some stuff to consider: - There is no way to reload a global plugin from code. https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13308 would resolve this though, so not sure if exposing a method for that is worth it. EDIT: There is also a really ugly workaround that allows it without a method. - ~If a global scene is open in 2 editor instances, editing the scene in one instance does not prompt scene change in the other instance.~ - Since UIDs exist for editor paths, it means they are likely in UID cache file, which means they get exported with the project. It would be nice to strip them probably.

Hi, Thank you for this! I've been looking for such a feature for years. I wonder if the files within global/editor plugins are still detected in the `Menu > Project > Tools > Orphan Resource Explorer`? Are they still resolved as dependencies if a file in a project refers to them? When exporting games, if options `Export selected scenes/resources (and dependencies)` are selected, do these files get exported with the built deliverables?

I'm also curious about how we are planning to manage the UIDs for the files across projects. Do they get a globally unique UID, or will they be local for each project?

> Hi, Thank you for this! I've been looking for such a feature for years. I wonder if the files within global/editor plugins are still detected in the `Menu > Project > Tools > Orphan Resource Explorer`? Are they still resolved as dependencies if a file in a project refers to them? When exporting games, if options `Export selected scenes/resources (and dependencies)` are selected, do these files get exported with the built deliverables?

Not sure about those, but what for sure is, the editor resources are meant to only be use for the editor, and not the project. So when exporting the game, theoretically the editor files should not be exported. You are not really supposed to mix up `res://` and `editor://` dependencies together in the first place anyway. Also, the `editor://` path prefix doesn't even work in running game, let alone the exported game.

> I'm also curious about how we are planning to manage the UIDs for the files across projects. Do they get a globally unique UID, or will they be local for each project?

They are global UIDs, same UIDs on all projects.

Also, the `editor://` path prefix doesn't even work in running game, let alone the exported game.
> 
> > I'm also curious about how we are planning to manage the UIDs for the files across projects. Do they get a globally unique UID, or will they be local for each project?
> 
> They are global UIDs, same UIDs on all projects.

Thank you for the clarification and I'm glad that we share the same idea for the expected behavior. This is exactly what I have always been wanting for godot—so we can have some pure dev dependencies that aren't exported with the package and the orphan resource explorer tool won't report them as orphans since they are intendedly not to be referenced by the main scene and its dependencies.

looking forward to seeing it being merged ❤️

Looks like most of my issues listed in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/119779#issuecomment-4886057169 have been resolved, the remaining ones aren't that much important. There is the case of warning button overlapping text when it's longer than "On" but that's a Tree bug, so unrelated. That leaves... > classes from an editor addon shouldn't appear by default in the Create node. It shoudl either be in the Editor Filter or in a new Custom Editor Filter Referencing a class or a path in "editor://" from "res://" or the reverse should result in a warning So, the problem with referencing `editor://` stuff in `res://` is that if you delete the referenced resource, some of your projects will "randomly" break. It won't cause corruption and the problem is generally recoverable, so it's not that bad. I think a warning in scene tree for `editor://` types and in GDScript could be helpful, but they are something that can be added later (especially GDScript warning might be more difficult). Referencing `res://` in `editor://` files, especially as dependencies, will make the global addon work only in a specific project, or with specific file structure. For scene dependencies, it might be fine to forbid it, if possible. For scripts, I think loading `res://` stuff is useful in case of file editors etc. Overall I think this PR might be more or less ready right now. Some details can be ironed out later.

I'm giving back a few feedback from my limited testing this morning but will comeback to do a longer review later today or in the following days.

I have looked into having multiple godot version and the current solution seems lacking. Rigth now it seems each version of godot has a fully different directory. This seems like a good idea at first because some plugin you might have installed on 4.9 might not work on 4.8 so you don't want it being enabled and creating errors. On the other hand this means that it breaks the idea that when you install there it is available for all your projects. it is blatantly flagrant when going up in version. The bare minimum would be on opening a new version to duplicate the previous version folder. But the better way would be to have only one folder for all and to have a minimum godot version (and maybe also maximum) the plugin supports. when the condition is not met the plugin is greyed out and is not enabled (with a warning explaining why). If I remember correctly ths information is already present in a way in the asset store so maybe it should be unified with that. 

I have looked into gdextensions too and they appear on the project settings tab maybe they should have a tab in editor plugins and appear there.

Also is there a reasons to go `editor://addons/addon-name/` instead of `editor://addon-name/`.

> Also is there a reasons to go editor://addons/addon-name/ instead of editor://addon-name/.

Consistency with project-wide addons, and it's required to have plugins that can be both local and global.
Also technically the global filesystem can be used for more than just addons.

> the better way would be to have only one folder for all and to have a minimum godot version (and maybe also maximum) the plugin supports.

That won't help if the resources are not compatible. Like, if an addon uses some new syntax or format not available in older versions, it's going to spam parse errors forever, because disabled addons can't be ignored completely.

We can add a migration option that copies addons between versions, but it won't be needed until next version, so there is no rush.

> Both options seem like they achieve the same thing at first, but they create the plugin in different locations on the filesystem.

Project settings always create plugins in `res://`, editor settings always create in `editor://`. "Project + editor" just means that the plugin can be moved from `res://` to `editor://` and vice versa. There is no difference where you create it originally.

About the asset store installation, can we do something as plugin developper to provide both a editor and runtime plugin where in the plugin the editor is quite large and don't need to be shipped in the game. Should we have 2 seperate plugin in the asset store with in one side the editor and the other side the runtime ? any "magic" folder name / property in the cfg file to tell the installer where to put the files ?
Or the plugin itself handle the moving file around in the correct folders ?

I haven't read the entire discussion here. But I'm missing clear documentation/specification on what is and isn't supported and how/if we do check that. I can't say if this would cause issues for GDS without knowing what this is supposed to support. Also this should not be an afterthought because there seems to be a lot of footgun potential, when project resources depend on a resource in `editor://`, so plugin devs must have documentation that outlines what they can and can't do (e.g. custom node types from an `editor://` plugin is probably a no-go). Also can someone tell me what I'm doing wrong here: I'm not able to create a global plugin. I also can't enable it after moving it manually.

> Also can someone tell me what I'm doing wrong here:

Global plugins are in editor settings.

> About the asset store installation, can we do something as plugin developper to provide both a editor and runtime plugin where in the plugin the editor is quite large and don't need to be shipped in the game.

Marking the plugin as both project and editor allows the user to install it in either place; on your side you only have to ensure that it works both as local and global.

Which I realized is not entirely possible right now .-. The problem is that scenes always use absolute paths to resources. They will load fine thanks to UIDs, but plugins out of original scope are always going to print warnings. We'd need support for relative dependency paths or `addon://` prefix, but that's likely out of scope for this PR.
This PR does allow `class_name` in `editor://`, why?

> About the asset store installation, can we do something as plugin developper to provide both a editor and runtime plugin where in the plugin the editor is quite large and don't need to be shipped in the game. Should we have 2 seperate plugin in the asset store with in one side the editor and the other side the runtime ? any "magic" folder name / property in the cfg file to tell the installer where to put the files ? Or the plugin itself handle the moving file around in the correct folders ?

I think if your goal is to have part as editor part as project you should have only an editor one which itself has a way to install ina project. Like when enabled and on a project it hasn't seen yet just popup a window asking wether the user want to install in this project or not.

I think the `Editor-wide and Project-wide` scope should be removed, since it is probably not going to be frequently used, and its going to create more problems than convenient.

The main issue is with the conflicts. If you have an addon installed on both project and editor, that will caused a UID and custom class conflict. Also, if you already have the addon on the editor side, then there's kind of no point of also having it on the project side.

Another issue is with project-editor compatibility, since scenes file normally stored resources using an absolute path, then it will not work if the addons is moved to a different path, i.e. project dir to editor dir.

Even if we add a new path protocol `addon://` that points to an addon folder, so all of the addon's content can use a path relative to it, this would only work if the addon is inside the addon folder, (not sure if it is encouraged to place your addon outside the `res://addons/` folder anyway, but its possible.)

All in all, I think we can just remove it, or at the very least, only for now. And if it is really needed we can just re add it again later.

What do you all think? Feel free to disagree with me if you got different opinions.

tbh I'm not sure where "Editor-wide and Project-wide" plugins come from in the current form. I get what they could be useful for and just rolled with it when reviewing, but the feature is questionable and has problems.

I did once mention "editor and runtime" plugins when global addons were discussed, but it was about plugins that are both. They can be global, but install some files in the project. However the addon itself would be qualified as global.

So yeah, the feature can be removed, or disabled for now (i.e. just remove menu options); either way is fine. The workaround for having plugins that can work in both contexts is submitting 2 versions to asset store - one global, and one for project. I do have a couple addons that can work like this.

Removed "Editor-wide and project-wide" scope. But now the scope options is awkward looking since it only have one selectable item: Not sure what to do about it. We could just remove this option entirely, but then the plugin scope cannot be changed if the scope is unknown or incompatible.
Improved tooltips: When creating a plugin: When editing a plugin:

> For readability purposes, we may want to store a string representing the enum value instead, similar to the stretch mode/aspect project settings. The rest of the file is very human-readable currently, so it's odd to have it stand out like that Added:

> This PR does allow class_name in editor://, why?

I think it's fine using class_name in editor, I don't see any problem with that. Though, maybe we should enforce the style of having "Editor" prefix on the class_name. That way it is more consistent with the built-in editor classes, and it is less likely to be mistaken for a project class.

> I don't see any problem with that.

One problem is that it makes scripts depend on another script somewhere in global filesystem. I'm not convinced on the "global plugin" terminology at all, mostly because we are going to introduce yet another meaning for what "global" entails in the engine. Keep in mind the following:
- **Global** transformations are relative to the world (unlike local transformations).
- For popup menus, shortcuts to "global" menu items are triggered even their popup menu is inaccessible (do correct me on this)
- For editor docks, "global" denotes docks which will appear in the **Editor > Editor Docks**
- There is an entire tab named "**Globals**" in the project settings
	- For nodes, a "global" group is defined in the project settings, unlike a "local" group.
	- Any autoloaded node can be a "Global variable" to make it accessible from any script.
	- "Global" shader parameters can be accessed on all shaders used in the project.
- Everything defined in `@GlobalScope` can be accessed from any script, at any point during execution.
- Absolute file paths are sometimes considered "global" (e.g. `ProjectSettings.globalize_path()`)
- "Global classes" can be accessed from any script.
- For EditorUndoRedoManager, the "global history" is used for anything not associated with any specific scene.
- For AnimationMixer, the "global library" is the name for the default library, used as a fallback (do correct me on this).
- "Global" illumination, as in, the rendering technique that affects the lighting of a whole scene.
- Etcetera.

As you can see, none of the terms using "global" have an effect across the entire editor. A lot of them also have "local" equivalents or ways to override the global definitions. Even then, they're still scoped within any individual project.
So overall, in my opinion, what "global" tends to stand for is: something at the top-most level that can be accessed from anywhere, or has an effect on everything, **within an individual project**.

According to https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_resourceloader.html#class-resourceloader-method-load and https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_%40gdscript.html#class-gdscript-method-load, they eventually become `res://` paths.

Relative paths are only supported for static loading, such as in `preload("icon.png")` and `extends "my_script.gd"`. They are not supported for dynamic loading, `load("icon.png")` is the same as `load("res://icon.png")`.
